data.title: Show HN: WebGPU enables local LLM in the browser – demo site with AI chat
data.author: andreinwald
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebLLM演示、模型性能及其实现技术细节

不同观点：
• [maxmcd] 指出该项目是基于https://github.com/mlc-ai/web-llm，并提供了一个完整的网页演示链接。
• [echoangle] 对模型的智能程度提出质疑，通过一个关于如何前往太空的回答示例，认为模型回答不够准确且信息过时。
• [scottfr] 提到正在开发的Prompt API，可以在Chrome和Edge中访问本地LLM，并提供了有关模型和测试版本的详细信息。
• [petermcneeley] 指出该演示仅在具备"f16"功能的webgpu上工作，并提供了检查功能的链接。
• [AndrewDucker] 报告了模型的输出异常问题，得到了无意义的字符串结果。
• [201984] 询问是否可以利用实际的GPU而非集成显卡来运行该演示。
• [andreinwald] 确认模型为Llama 3.2 1B，并指出其质量与Ollama应用类似。
• [dataviz1000] 对演示表示赞赏，并提供了更多在webgpu上运行不同模型的示例链接。
• [asim] 对模型性能与OpenAI API进行了比较，并询问了模型性能的限制因素。
• [gulan28] 提到曾在https://wiz.chat上做过类似项目，并警告该项目需要较大的模型和GPU支持，且仅在Chrome上工作。
• [apitman] 询问为什么WebGPU LLM演示需要将模型下载到浏览器存储中，而不是使用本地驱动器上的模型。
• [om8] 提到GPU推理需要实际的GPU，并提供了一个运行8B llama的演示链接。
• [cat-whisperer] 对WebGPU的发展及其潜在应用表示关注，认为该演示展示了其可能性。
• [cgdl] 询问演示所使用的具体模型。
• [RagnarD] 认为该演示想法不错，但存在一些问题，经过简单测试发现有故障。

补充讨论：
• 模型性能和输出质量是讨论的重点，部分用户对模型的智能程度和准确性提出质疑。
• 技术实现细节，特别是关于GPU使用、模型下载和存储的讨论，反映了用户对实际运行效果和可行性的关注。
• 不同用户提供了多个相关项目和资源的链接，展示了社区对该技术的兴趣和参与。
• 争议的焦点在于模型的质量和演示的稳定性，部分用户报告了异常结果和功能性问题。

data.title: Financial lessons from my family's experience with long-term care insurance
data.author: wallflower
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在2024年1月经历的父亲因痴呆症走失并被送往医院的事件，以及之后处理父亲长期护理保险（LTC）索赔的过程。作者的父亲被诊断出患有轻度认知障碍，但在一次意外走失后，确诊为痴呆症，家庭意识到他无法再独自生活。幸运的是，作者的父母早年购买了长期护理保险，这为后续的护理费用提供了保障。作者分享了索赔过程中的经验，强调要直接联系保险公司获取申请表，并提到保险公司会进行独立评估。作者还建议尽可能找到保险公司呼叫中心的联系人，以加快沟通。本文为有类似情况的家庭提供了实用的指导。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国医疗保健系统的问题及相关解决方案

不同观点：
• [lvl155] 认为美国的医疗系统存在多重复杂的激励机制，导致系统无法有效运作。特别是药品福利管理公司（PBMs）激励药物价格上涨，建议通过迁移到其他国家或成为低收入者以获得医疗支持。
• [shirleyglvins] 分享了个人经历，提到一种特定的多发性硬化症治疗方法（MS-4 Protocol）对其症状有显著改善，但担心评论会被视为垃圾信息。
• [WarOnPrivacy] 提出通过移除分区障碍来允许辅助居住单元（ADU）的建设，可以为家庭和住房供应带来好处。
• [mhb] 指出保险公司对家庭健康护理提供者的支付限制导致难以找到合适的护理人员。
• [FloatArtifact] 提到在一些州，长期护理保险可以保护资产，从而有资格获得医疗补助，同时保留一定的资产用于其他需求。
• [narrator] 建议雇佣护理人员在家中照顾病人，而不是在护理机构，这样既节省成本，护理人员也能获得更高收入和激励。

By
Adam Safdi
, WCI Columnist
On January 31, 2024, I received a call at 4am from a strange number. Normally, I keep my phone on vibrate overnight, but this number kept calling repeatedly. Eventually, I woke up and answered the phone. The caller said, “Adam? This is Adam, right? This is Jack, a friend of your dad. I’m sorry to call so early, but I have some distressing news.”
Jack went on to tell me that the police were taking my dad to the local hospital’s emergency department. Over the next few hours, we pieced together the story. My dad had wandered out of his house the night before, presumably to go for a walk. It started raining, and he became disoriented, unable to find his way home. He found a house with an unlocked door and went inside. He fell asleep in a spare bedroom. When he woke early the next morning, he became frustrated and confused by his unfamiliar surroundings.
The couple who lived there found him wandering in their kitchen. After the initial shock, they realized my dad posed no threat, but they called 911 due to the intrusion. No charges were filed, and the police recognized what our family had feared for some time: dementia. The local ER staff evaluated him for acute medical issues, and after finding nothing urgent, they sent him home.
I must first publicly express my gratitude to the couple who found my dad. I can only imagine how distressing it must have been to find a stranger in their home. I sent them a letter thanking them for their kindness and understanding.
Let me explain a little bit about my father’s situation. My mother passed away in 2018, and my father has lived alone since. He has a new girlfriend who lives 30 minutes away. My brother lives two hours away, and I live three time zones away. Up until that point, we knew he had some memory difficulties, and a local neurologist had diagnosed him with mild cognitive impairment.
But we didn’t think it was that severe.
There had been instances where my dad chose mismatched or inappropriate clothing, burned his toast, or replaced the telephone in the refrigerator instead of on the phone charger. However, after the January 2024 incident, we went back to his neurologist, who sadly confirmed that with my dad’s combination of cognitive and functional impairments—most notably his lack of direction, wandering, and getting lost—meant that he had progressed from mild cognitive impairment to dementia. It became clear that my dad was likely no longer safe to be by himself at home.
While my dad was the breadwinner during his working years, my mother managed the household finances. She and my father had bought
long-term care (LTC) insurance
policies for the possibility of prolonged illness later in life. As best as I can tell from the paperwork, my parents bought these policies in 2004, they each paid about $14,000 in annual premiums for 10 years, and the daily benefit started at $200 per day. I was unaware of these policies when my mother died (after a relatively short illness), but I became aware of them when an uncle called and mentioned, “Your father has a long-term care insurance policy. I helped him get it.”
Thus began the long process of filing and obtaining claims with the LTC insurance company. I’d like to share some lessons learned from this experience.
What to Do with Your Relative's Long-Term Care Insurance
#1 Call the Insurance Company to Obtain an Application to File a Claim
For a while, my brother and I tried to track down the actual policy. We sifted through stacks of paperwork at our dad’s house and became frustrated (fairly and unfairly) that he didn’t know where the papers were located. When we finally called the insurance company, it, of course, had his policy on file. The company sent us an application, and we began filling out the paperwork. The application included several parts:
Authorization to obtain and disclose information
Claimant’s statement
Attending physician’s statement
Benefit direct deposit form
Fraud notice
Try to get a point of contact in the company's call center if possible. We found calling more fruitful than emailing. Many of our emails went completely unanswered, which was a source of frustration and delayed the process.
More information here:
The Challenges of Long-Distance Eldercare
Cost of Caring for Aging Parents
#2 Insurance Companies Do Their Own Evaluations

data.title: Double-slit experiment holds up when stripped to its quantum essentials
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: MIT物理学家通过精简的双缝实验证实了光的波粒二象性，这一量子特性在同一时刻无法同时观察到。实验使用两个单原子作为双缝，通过激光照射，并用高敏感度相机记录散射光的干涉图样。当尝试测量光子路径时，光的波动性消失，显示粒子特性，反之亦然。该实验源自1801年托马斯·杨的双缝实验，证明光同时具有波和粒子的性质，但无法同时展现这两种特性。爱因斯坦曾对这一量子现象持不同看法，但实验结果支持了尼尔斯·波尔的观点，验证了量子力学的基本原理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：双缝实验及其相关量子现象的解释与技术细节

不同观点：
• [habibur] 对量子擦除实验中光子行为的兴趣，特别是光子在通过狭缝并击中探测器后，依据后续决定改变其历史行为的观点。支持这一观点的例子是延迟选择量子擦除实验，强调光子似乎会根据后来的决定回溯改变历史。

• [gronglo] 质疑探测器的类型对实验结果的影响，提出不同的探测器可能会对实验结果产生显著影响，并认为科普解释中通常忽略这一细节。

• [gwerbret] 质疑新研究的创新性，认为该研究只是对30多年前实验的重新分析，并提供了一个1993年的研究链接以支持其观点。

• [cluckindan] 提出光子传播和离散事件之间的关系，认为光子作为无质量的非局域波传播，但在与有质量的粒子碰撞时变得局部化，强调电磁辐射的连续性与量子事件的离散性。

• [mhb] 提供了一个关于量子干涉的参考链接，试图通过具体例子解释量子现象。

• [briffid] 对波粒二象性的理解提出疑问，质疑光子是否按百分比表现出波动性和粒子性，并对其解释的清晰性表示困惑。

• [moktonar] 简单地提出模拟回滚以匹配约束条件的观点，暗示实验结果可以通过模拟技术进行解释。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到量子力学的复杂性和反直觉性，尤其是时间回溯和波粒二象性的问题。
• 技术细节如探测器的类型对实验结果的影响也被提出，显示出对实验方法和设备细节的关注。
• 对新研究的创新性存在争议，部分评论者认为该研究没有新的实质内容，而其他人则关注其解释和应用。
• 不同评论者对量子现象的理解和解释存在差异，反映出量子力学在大众理解中的多样性和复杂性。

Their findings demonstrate, with atomic-level precision, the dual yet evasive nature of light. They also happen to confirm that Albert Einstein was wrong about this particular quantum scenario.
The experiment in question is the
double-slit experiment
, which was first performed in 1801 by the British scholar Thomas Young to show how light behaves as a wave. Today, with the formulation of quantum mechanics, the double-slit experiment is now known for its surprisingly simple demonstration of a head-scratching reality: that light exists as both a particle and a wave. Stranger still, this duality cannot be simultaneously observed. Seeing light in the form of particles instantly obscures its wave-like nature, and vice versa.
The original experiment involved shining a beam of light through two parallel slits in a screen and observing the pattern that formed on a second, faraway screen. One might expect to see two overlapping spots of light, which would imply that light exists as particles, a.k.a. photons, like paintballs that follow a direct path. But instead, the light produces alternating bright and dark stripes on the screen, in an interference pattern similar to what happens when two ripples in a pond meet. This suggests light behaves as a wave. Even weirder, when one tries to measure which slit the light is traveling through, the light suddenly behaves as particles and the interference pattern disappears.
The double-slit experiment is taught today in most high school physics classes as a simple way to illustrate the fundamental principle of quantum mechanics: that all physical objects, including light, are simultaneously particles and waves.

In response, Bohr applied the quantum mechanical uncertainty principle and showed that the detection of the photon’s path would wash out the interference pattern.

data.article_summary:
**LangExtract** 是一个 Python 库，利用大型语言模型（LLMs）从非结构化文本中提取结构化信息，支持精确的源文本映射和交互式可视化。其主要特点包括：

1. **精确源映射**：提取的信息映射回源文本的准确位置，支持高亮显示以方便验证。
2. **可靠的结构化输出**：基于少量示例强制执行一致的输出模式，确保结果的稳健性。
3. **长文档优化**：通过文本分块、并行处理和多轮提取策略，解决大文档提取的难题。
4. **交互式可视化**：生成自包含的交互式 HTML 文件，方便查看提取结果。
5. **灵活的LLM支持**：支持云端模型（如Google Gemini）和本地开源模型。
6. **领域适应性强**：通过少量示例定义提取任务，无需模型微调。

使用时，用户通过定义提示和示例来指导模型，并调用 `lx.extract` 函数进行提取。推荐使用 `gemini-2.5-flash` 模型以平衡速度、成本和质量。

Introduction
LangExtract is a Python library that uses LLMs to extract structured information from unstructured text documents based on user-defined instructions. It processes materials such as clinical notes or reports, identifying and organizing key details while ensuring the extracted data corresponds to the source text.
Why LangExtract?
Precise Source Grounding:
Maps every extraction to its exact location in the source text, enabling visual highlighting for easy traceability and verification.
Reliable Structured Outputs:
Enforces a consistent output schema based on your few-shot examples, leveraging controlled generation in supported models like Gemini to guarantee robust, structured results.
Optimized for Long Documents:
Overcomes the "needle-in-a-haystack" challenge of large document extraction by using an optimized strategy of text chunking, parallel processing, and multiple passes for higher recall.
Interactive Visualization:
Instantly generates a self-contained, interactive HTML file to visualize and review thousands of extracted entities in their original context.
Flexible LLM Support:
Supports your preferred models, from cloud-based LLMs like the Google Gemini family to local open-source models via the built-in Ollama interface.
Adaptable to Any Domain:
Define extraction tasks for any domain using just a few examples. LangExtract adapts to your needs without requiring any model fine-tuning.
Leverages LLM World Knowledge:
Utilize precise prompt wording and few-shot examples to influence how the extraction task may utilize LLM knowledge. The accuracy of any inferred information and its adherence to the task specification are contingent upon the selected LLM, the complexity of the task, the clarity of the prompt instructions, and the nature of the prompt examples.
Quick Start
Note:
Using cloud-hosted models like Gemini requires an API key. See the
API Key Setup
section for instructions on how to get and configure your key.

data

data.title: A Real PowerBook: The Macintosh Application Environment on a Pa-RISC Laptop
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了1997年时，RDI公司推出的一款基于PA-RISC架构的PrecisionBook笔记本电脑，与当时苹果和摩托罗拉主导的PowerPC架构的PowerBook形成对比。尽管Motorola 68000系列的后续通常被认为是PowerPC，但Commodore曾计划使用PA-RISC架构开发Amiga后续产品。RDI的PrecisionBook配备160MHz PA-7300LC处理器，拥有更高的分辨率、更大的内存和硬盘容量，支持HP-UX和Mac 68K软件，价格高达12,000美元。文章还回顾了RDI公司历史，其最初生产SPARC架构笔记本，后因市场变化转向PA-RISC。尽管PrecisionBook性能强劲，但因价格高昂和市场竞争，未能广泛普及。文章最后探讨了如果PowerBook基于PA-RISC，是否会成为一种更具性价比的选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple的Mac OS与Unix系统的兼容性及技术实现，以及对A/UX的历史和市场看法。

不同观点：
• [技术细节关注 - nxobject] 评论者关注Macintosh Application Environment (MAE) 如何通过各种技术手段将运行中的系统与主机操作系统集成。具体提到使用Quadra ROM、System Enabler和Helper应用，以及Toolbox UI服务的实现细节，包括对Toolbox的修补和调用主机OS服务。评论者还提出了一些未解之谜，例如在没有SCSI设备和ATA/IDE管理器的情况下如何实现磁盘访问和转换，以及是否对File Manager和68k模拟器进行了大量修补。

• [历史和市场视角 - pjmlp] 评论者讨论了Apple在UNIX领域的历史，特别是A/UX和NeXT之间的关系。提到Steve Jobs对UNIX并不热衷，以及NeXT通过吸引UNIX用户和客户来推广NeXTSTEP。还提到OpenSTEP的努力和与Sun的合作是在销售不如预期后开始的。最后，评论者分享了自己在1994年IT会议上见到A/UX的经历，认为它看起来很有趣。

补充讨论：
• [MAE的技术实现 - ethan_smith] 评论者简要描述了MAE是Apple尝试在Unix工作站上运行Mac OS，创建了一个兼容层将Mac Toolbox调用转换为X11，使Unix用户能够在不使用Apple硬件的情况下运行Mac软件。

• [怀旧和技术历史 - esafak] 评论者提到PA-RISC架构，回忆起自己年轻时向HP索要相关资料的经历，感叹HP曾经是强有力的竞争者。

• [幽默和文化参考 - Telemakhos] 评论者幽默地将RISC Mac与经典电影《Mission Impossible》联系起来，暗示实现RISC Mac的难度和不可能性。

争议焦点：
• 对A/UX和UNIX的历史发展及市场策略有不同看法，尤其是Jobs对UNIX的态度以及NeXT和Apple之间的策略关系。

总结：讨论涉及技术细节、历史背景和个人怀旧情感，展示了不同评论者对Apple技术实现和市场策略的多角度理解。

44774567.article_content:
I like the Power ISA very much, but there's nothing architecturally obvious to say that the next natural step from the Motorola 68000 family must be to PowerPC. For example, the Palm OS
moved from the DragonBall to ARM
, and it's not necessarily a well-known fact that the successor to Commodore's 68K Amigas was intended to be based on PA-RISC, Hewlett-Packard's "Precision Architecture" processor family. (That was
the Hombre chipset
, and
prototype chips existed
prior to Commodore's demise in 1994, though controversy swirled regarding backwards compatibility.) Sure, Apple and Motorola were two-thirds of the AIM alliance, and there were several PowerPC PowerBooks available when the fall of 1997 rolled around. But what if the next PowerBooks had been based on PA-RISC instead?
Well, no need to strain yourself imagining it. Here's nearly as close as you're gonna get.
In October 1997 you could have bought a PowerBook 3400c running up to a 240MHz PowerPC 603e for $6500 [about $13,000 in 2025 dollars], which was briefly billed as the world's fastest laptop, or you could have bought this monster new to the market, the RDI PrecisionBook running up to a 160MHz (later 180MHz) PA-7300LC starting at $12,000 [$24,000]. Both provided onboard Ethernet, SCSI and CardBus PCMCIA slots. On the other hand, while the 3400c had an internal media bay for either a floppy or CD-ROM, both external options on the PrecisionBook, the PrecisionBook gave you a 1024x768 LCD (versus 800x600 on the 3400c), a bigger keyboard, at least two 2.5" hard disk bays and up to 512MB of RAM (versus 144MB) — and HP-UX.
And, through the magic of Apple's official Macintosh Application Environment, you could do anything on it an HP PA-RISC workstation could do and run 68K Mac software on it at the same time. Look at the photograph and see: on our 160MHz unit we've got HP-UX 11.00 CDE running simultaneously with a full Macintosh System 7.5.3 desktop. Yes, only a real Power Mac could run PowerPC software back then, but 68K software was still plentiful and functional. Might this have been a viable option to have your expensive cake and eat it too? We'll find out and run some real apps on it (including
that
game we must all try running), analyze its performance and technical underpinnings, and uncover an unusual artifact of its history hidden in the executable.
(A shout-out to Paul Weissman, the author and maintainer of the incomparable PA-RISC resource
OpenPA.net
, who provided helpful insights for this article.)
In this entry the hardware is at least as unusual as the software we'll be running on it, so let's start with the story of the hardware since it's a bit shorter. Yet another computer manufacturer
near my childhood hometown
, RDI Computer Systems was founded in 1989 as Research, Development and Innovations Incorporated in La Costa, California, a neighbourhood of Carlsbad annexed in 1972 in northern San Diego county.
(It is completely unrelated to earlier Carlsbad company RDI
Video
Systems, short for "Rick Dyer Industries" and the developers of laserdisc games like
Dragon's Lair
and
Space Ace
, who folded in 1985 after their expensive Halcyon home console imploded mid-development from the 1983 video game crash.)
RDI, like several of its contemporaries, was established to capitalize on Sun Microsystems' attempt to commoditize SPARC and open up the market to other OEMs. While most such vendors like
Solbourne Computer
heavily invested in the desktop workstation segment, RDI instead went even smaller, producing what would become the first SPARC laptops in the United States. Basically SPARCstation IPC and IPX systems crammed into boxy off-white portable cases, the BriteLite series weighed a bit over 13 pounds and started at $10,000 [$24,600]. They were lauded for their performance and compatibility but not their battery life, and RDI became an early adopter of Sun's lower-power microSPARC for the sleeker, sexier PowerLites, using a more dramatic jet-black case. An 85MHz microSPARC II PowerLite 85 was the machine that computational physicist Tsutomu Shimomura, then at the San Diego Supercomputer Center, used to track down hacker Kevin Mitnick in 1995.
RDI's initial success enabled its expansion into a bigger 40,000-square foot industrial park facility at 2300 Faraday Avenue, which apparently still exists today. Unfortunately for the company, however, microSPARC hit a performance wall above 125MHz and Sun abandoned further development in 1994, which RDI management took as an indication they needed to diversify. By then the RISC market had started to flourish with many architectures competing for dominance, and RDI decided to throw in with Hewlett-Packard's PA-RISC which had extant portable systems already from Hitachi
and SAIC
. Neither of those systems had ever existed in large numbers (and the SAIC Galaxys only in military applications at that), giving RDI a new market opportunity with a respected architecture that was already mobile-capable. Producing a fin

data.title: Build Your Own Minisforum N5 Inspired Mini NAS
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NAS（网络附加存储）构建的选择、优缺点以及替代方案

不同观点：
• **diggan**：计划在发布几个月后公开Shapr3D设计文件，以便在公开之前解决潜在问题。同时，寻求其他3D打印NAS机箱的灵感。
• **bane**：支持使用便宜的4-bay Mediasonic Proboxes，认为这些设备性价比高，性能稳定，且比一体化NAS系统更具扩展性和持久性。
• **zevon**：使用旧笔记本和随机硬盘作为NAS，赞赏这种便宜且有效的方案。
• **choonway**：认为文中的NAS方案已经过时，推荐更强大且具备更多功能的设备，如Aoostar WTR Max。
• **noelwelsh**：正在考虑构建NAS，发现此文章开启了新的思路，并参考了其他构建方案。
• **rusk**：认为NAS构建不仅在于硬件，软件调试同样重要，最终选择购买一体化NAS以避免软件问题。
• **poemxo**：对文章中Noctua风扇的展示方式表示不满，希望有JBOD版本以配合Mac Mini使用，并对价格表示疑虑。
• **bsder**：对使用打印塑料材料制作NAS机箱表示兴趣，认为主要问题在于成本。
• **pama**：质疑为何需要高性能NAS，认为Raspberry Pi 5可能足够。
• **superkuh**：提出不构建NAS，直接将硬盘安装在常用电脑中，认为这样更具价格、性能和可靠性优势。
• **ggm**：关注m.2到SATA适配器的磁盘IO性能，分享了自己的类似构建方案，使用zimablade和PCI卡。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：NAS构建的必要性和性价比。部分用户（如bane）认为自己构建更具优势，而rusk和superkuh则认为一体化NAS或直接使用电脑更方便。
• **硬件选择**：不同用户推荐了多种硬件方案，从便宜的Mediasonic Proboxes到高性能的Aoostar WTR Max，以及Raspberry Pi 5。
• **软件调试**：rusk强调了NAS软件调试的复杂性，推荐一体化软件解决方案如unRAID。
• **性能与成本**：讨论中多次提到性能与成本的平衡，特别是高性能NAS是否必要以及便宜方案的可行性。

这些观点展示了NAS构建中的多样化选择和个人偏好，以及硬件和软件方面的考虑。

data.author: domofutu
data.article_summary: 文章揭示了北卡罗来纳州许多高分学生未被安排进高级数学课程的问题。研究发现，超过一半有望在高级数学中成功的学生未被安排进这些课程，尤其是一些低收入和少数族裔学生，尽管他们成绩优异。传统上，高级数学课程需要教师推荐，但数据表明许多高分学生并未获得推荐。2009年的一项分析显示，约35,000名初中生本应在8年级学习代数，但未被安排，尽管他们在9年级代数考试中表现优异。文章指出，这种系统性问题浪费了大量学生潜力。一些学校通过取消教师推荐要求，让高分学生进入高级课程，结果证明这些学生能够成功适应高级课程。文章呼吁改革数学课程安排，确保高分学生有机会接受更具挑战性的教育。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国中学数学课程安排的现状及其问题，特别是代数I课程的获取和高级课程的推荐机制。

不同观点：
• rahimnathwani：指出旧金山数学课程安排存在问题，八年级学生很难在学年内获得面对面的代数I课程，尽管该地区每个学生的平均运营支出很高。
• djoldman：认为通过教师推荐来决定学生是否能上高级课程会导致偏见，并提到北卡罗来纳州通过的法律，要求标准化测试高分学生自动进入高级课程，以此解决偏见问题。他还指出人类判断常常出错，暗示自动化可能有帮助。
• recursivecaveat：对将高级数学课程视为稀缺资源感到不满，认为这种做法会导致教育上的不平等，即“有”和“没有”的状况。
• vorgol：质疑如果不掌握代数，如何能学习高级数学，暗示代数是基础。
• zozbot234：认为将代数I视为“高级”数学是美国特有的问题，在欧洲和东亚并不存在，称其为“低期望的软性偏见”。
• chriscrisby：提出是否研究了那些数学好但不感兴趣的学生的情况，质疑是否所有学生都应被推向高级课程。
• thevillagechief：对美国通过行政和家长干预限制学生选择课程的做法感到沮丧，指出大多数国家没有这种高级课程分级制度，认为这是精英阶层维护自身优势的手段。
• anovikov：认为有限的教育资源应优先分配给更有可能在生活中应用这些知识的学生，暗示资源分配应考虑实际需求。
• elric：反驳大规模未能上高级课程就是浪费人类潜力的说法，认为未上代数课程的学生可能在其他课程上表现良好，不认为这是人生失败或浪费潜力的表现。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于高级数学课程的获取和分配机制，特别是在推荐机制中的人类偏见问题，以及是否应将高级课程视为稀缺资源进行分配。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是资源分配的公平性和效率问题，以及不同国家教育制度的对比。
• 对于是否所有学生都应被推向高级课程，存在分歧，部分人认为应尊重学生的兴趣和选择，而不是强制所有人都上高级课程。

How schools deny advanced math to their highest-scoring students

More than half of students predicted to succeed in advanced math are denied access to those classes.
Our research firm evaluates federally funded education programs in K-12 schools. In the early to mid-2000s, these grant-funded program evaluations began requiring measurable objectives and pre- and post-data comparisons. During this period, federal grants aimed at getting more low-income and minority students into advanced STEM courses became a common trend.
These program evaluation requirements led to a striking discovery. Tens of thousands of high-scoring students in North Carolina were not enrolled in advanced math courses. When staff working on the grant-funded programs (typically school counselors, school improvement teams, and administrators) discovered they already had hundreds of top-scoring, academically successful students in a single middle or high school who were not in advanced math, they usually wanted to enroll them. More often than not, they were told by their math departments that they couldn't enroll these students because students needed a teacher recommendation.
Educators involved in these grant-funded programs became curious about who was actually enrolled in advanced math and how those students had gained access. They asked us to examine the data to find out, as they had simply assumed that the students with the highest math scores were the ones in advanced math classes. Very few low-income and minority students were enrolled in advanced math, and the school counselors and administrators assumed this was because these students didn't score high on assessments. This incorrect assumption led them to write objectives for their grant-funded programs focused on increasing the number of low-income and minority students who scored high in math, believing there were virtually none. They had also incorrectly assumed that if their grant-funded services resulted in these students scoring higher that they would enroll in advanced math.
Subscribe
When academic achievement and advanced enrollment diverge
In 2009, North Carolina administrators were becoming more aware that enrollment in advanced math classes was not done by academic achievement, largely due to the new trend of federal grants aimed at increasing enrollment of low-income and minority students. The North Carolina Association of School Administrators hired us to work with SAS to investigate how math placement related to math achievement in all school districts in the state.
SAS Institute analyzed academic scores and math course enrollment patterns for all of North Carolina and for each school system.
SAS Institute
is a leading global provider of advanced analytics and statistical software, with over 12,000 employees and more than 80,000 customer sites in 140 countries, making it a major player in enterprise data solutions across industry and academia. Their analysis revealed the extent of these placement gaps. Among 7th graders with strong statistical predictions for success in advanced math, fewer than 50% were actually placed in 8th-grade algebra. At the same time, many students in those advanced classes had lower success predictions than students who were not recommended for the class.
This is not a small problem affecting a few students. This analysis revealed a systematic failure affecting tens of thousands of children across North Carolina alone, wasting human potential on a massive scale. The study done in 2009 showed that about 35,000 North Carolina middle school students were predicted to be successful in 8th-grade algebra but were not enrolled. They went on to take 9th-grade algebra, and more than 25,000 of them scored at the highest level on the 9th-grade algebra end-of-grade test. Yet despite this demonstrated high performance, they remained in the standard track rather than advancing to more rigorous mathematics courses, such as Honors, Advanced Placement, or IB math classes.
1
In some schools that we worked with, either evaluating their grants or helping them with their school improvement plans, principals overrode the typical placement requirement of teacher recommendations and enrolled all high-scoring students into the advanced math track. If we were working on the evaluation of a grant-funded program we would follow the students’ progress over several years. Nearly all students who were moved to the advanced math track based on their academic scores were successful in earning As or Bs in the courses and remained on the advanced track. data.title: 2,500-year-old Siberian 'ice mummy' had intricate tattoos, imaging reveals
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 高分辨率影像揭示了一具2500年前的西伯利亚“冰尸”身上的复杂纹身。这具女性木乃伊属于游牧民族帕兹里克人，其纹身包括豹、鹿、公鸡以及狮身鹰首兽等神话生物，展示了古代战士文化的艺术风格。通过与纹身艺术家的合作，研究人员发现这些纹身技艺精湛，可能使用了多点和单点工具以及植物烧成的颜料。纹身质量在两只手臂上有所不同，可能由不同人完成或因失误导致。研究还表明，纹身可能在生前具有重要意义，而在死后并不重要。这些发现发表在《古代》期刊上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：古代纹身的艺术性、历史背景及其文化意义

不同观点：
• **topspin** 认为这些纹身展现了比中世纪绘画更好的透视、动态和比例表达，强调这是真正的艺术，尤其考虑到这些纹身是在皮肤上而非纸张上。
• **romanhn** 指出木乃伊纹身早已为人所知，但对研究员 Daniel Riday 使用历史方法在身上重现古代纹身设计表示惊讶，认为这是对研究的高度奉献。
• **VTimofeenko** 分享了其祖父在苏联时期于西伯利亚北部工作时的见闻，提到面部纹身在一些地区是宗教和地位的象征，并质疑这种传统如何在不同地区传播。
• **jcmontx** 提到斯基泰木乃伊纹身，认为其具有艺术价值，例如纹有花朵的鹿。
• **koevet** 表达了对 Pazyryk 木乃伊纹身风格的强烈情感连接，并计划继续纹身以复制这些古代设计。
• **userbinator** 关注图像是否经过“AI增强”处理，并对使用的后期处理方法表示好奇。
• **casenmgreen** 认为公元前500年的纹身艺术相对较近，并对比同时期希腊和西伯利亚文化的“先进性”，指出纹身和艺术较易发展，而商业、建筑和军事组织等更为复杂。
• **dclowd9901** 反驳文章中关于现代纹身艺术家难以复制古代纹身的观点，认为现代优秀纹身艺术家在技术和艺术上都非常出色。
• **treis** 质疑如何确定这些是纹身而非死后绘制的图案。

补充讨论：
• **lupusreal** 指出纹身中的格里芬图案有翅膀，并引用了希腊和罗马文献中关于格里芬的描述，讨论其与中亚金矿的关联，提供历史背景。
• **apwell23** 提到最近在一个播客中听到相关内容，提供额外信息来源。
• **Theodores** 讨论了纹身在现代社会中的流行及其历史演变，指出纹身文化的普及与互联网及技术进步的关系，并从社会经济角度分析纹身文化，认为古代有纹身文化的社会相对不 primitive，因为它们能够支持专门职业和阶层。
• **giardini** 开玩笑说古代纹身者可能死于肝炎，暗示古代纹身的卫生问题。
• **wileydragonfly** 质疑从2500年前的遗体中能学到什么有价值的知识，并认为应尊重死者，将其安葬。

争议焦点：
• 古代纹身的艺术价值及其与现代纹身艺术的比较。
• 如何确定纹身的真实性及其文化意义。
• 从古代遗体中获取知识的伦理问题。

44745441.article_content:
2,500-year-old Siberian 'ice mummy' had intricate tattoos, imaging reveals
4 days ago
Share
Save
Georgina Rannard
Science correspondent
Share
Save
G Caspari and M Vavulin
Scans of the ice mummy's skin revealed details of animals and birds on her arms and hands
High-resolution imaging of tattoos found on a 2,500 year old Siberian "ice mummy" have revealed decorations that a modern tattooist would find challenging to produce, according to researchers.
The intricate tattoos of leopards, a stag, a rooster, and a mythical half-lion and half-eagle creature on the woman's body shed light on an ancient warrior culture.
Archaeologists worked with a tattooist, who reproduces ancient skin decorations on his own body, to understand how exactly they were made.
The tattooed woman, aged about 50, was from the nomadic horse-riding Pazyryk people who lived on the vast steppe between China and Europe.
Daniel Riday
An illustration of the tattoo on the woman's right forearm revealed in new scans
The scans revealed "intricate crisp and uniform" tattooing that could not be seen with the naked eye.
"The insights really drive home to me the point of how sophisticated these people were," lead author Dr Gino Caspari from the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology and the University of Bern, told BBC News.
It is difficult to uncover detailed information about ancient social and cultural practices because most evidence is destroyed over time. It is even harder to get up close to the details of one person's life.
The Pazyryk "ice mummies" were found inside ice tombs in the Altai mountains in Siberia in the 19th century, but it has been difficult to see the tattoos.
Daniel Riday
An illustration of the tattoo on the woman's left forearm revealed in new scans
Now using near-infrared digital photography in the Hermitage Museum in St Petersburg, Russia experts have created high resolution scans of the decorations for the first time.
"This made me feel like we were much closer to seeing the people behind the art, how they worked and learned. The images came alive," Dr Caspari said.
On her right forearm, the Pazyryk woman had an image of leopards around the head of a deer.
Getty Images
The Pazyryk were a nomadic group that lived in the Altai mountains
On the left arm, the mythical griffin creature with the body of a lion and the head and wings of an eagle appears to be fighting with a stag.
"Twisted hind bodies and really intense battle scenes of wild animals are typical of the culture," Dr Caspari said.
But the woman also had a rooster on her thumb, showing "an intriguing style with a certain uniqueness," says Dr Caspari.
The team worked with researcher Daniel Riday who reproduces ancient tattoo designs on his body using historical methods.
Daniel Riday
Daniel Riday uses pre-electric methods to tattoo ancient decorations on his skin
A 'solid commitment'
His insights on the scans led them to conclude that the quality of the work differed between the two arms, suggesting that a different person made the tattoos or that mistakes were made.
"If I was guessing, it was probably four and half hours for the lower half of the right arm, and another five hours for the upper part," he says.
"That's a solid commitment from the person. Imagine sitting on the ground in the steppe where there's wind blowing all that time," he suggests.
"It would need to be performed by a person who knows health and safety, who knows the risks of what happens when the skin is punctured," he adds.
High-resolution scans and images of the woman's skin give insights into the tattoo method
By analysing the marks in the woman's skin, the team believe that the tattoos were probably stencilled onto the skin before being tattooed.
They think a needle-like tool with small multiple points probably made from animal horn or bone was used, as well as a single point needle. The pigment was likely made from burnt plant material or soot.
Dr Caspari, who does not have tattoos himself, says the work sheds light on an ancient practice that is very important for a lot of people around the world today.
Daniel Riday
An illustration of the tattoo on the woman's thumb and fingers
"And back in the day it was already a really professional practice where people put a lot of time and effort and practice into creating these images and they're extremely sophisticated," he adds.
Some of the tattoos appear to have been cut or damaged when the body was prepared for burial.
"It suggests that tattoos were really something for the living with meaning during life, but that they actually didn't really play much of a role in the afterlife," explains Dr Caspari.
The findings are published in the journal Antiquity.
M Vavulin
Several ice mummies were found in the Altai mountains and they are currently kept at the Hermitage Museum in Russia

data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: D. Sculley，谷歌剑桥机器学习团队负责人，参与一个涉及机器学习在设计和制造领域应用的课程。他对跨领域机会特别感兴趣，包括生物学和化学空间。Sculley自2003年开始从事机器学习，之前有教育和艺术背景。课程为期14周，每周聚焦不同主题，从CAD和草图设计到嵌入式编程、网络、机械加工等，最终完成一个项目。Sculley计划每周参与项目，乐于讨论机器学习相关问题。

主要讨论点：围绕MIT的"How to Make Almost Anything"课程及其相关内容的讨论，涉及课程内容、个人制造能力、技能广度与深度等。

不同观点：
• [支持与赞赏课程]
  ◦ [criddell] 认为这是个人制造的黄金时代，高品质的个人制造能力已经实现，Neil Gershenfeld的预言正在成真。
  ◦ [zakqwy] 以亲身经历表示该课程非常有趣，涵盖了数字制造和微控制器等内容。
  ◦ [jeffreyw128] 表示这是他大学期间最喜欢的课程。
  ◦ [low_tech_punk] 和 [sgnelson] 提供了课程的链接和进一步资源，强调学生文档和项目是课程亮点。

• [对课程内容的批评与扩展建议]
  ◦ [moron4hire] 批评课程缺乏基础技能如木工、金属加工、管道、混凝土等，认为课程视野狭窄，并指出科技行业过度贬低年长者的技能和经验。
  ◦ [probably_wrong] 认为课程遗漏了缝纫等技能，建议将课程名称改为"How to make some things (most of which require a computer)"。

• [个人经验与反思]
  ◦ [dhosek] 后悔在本科期间没有选修某些实践类课程，如自制工具课程。
  ◦ [Animats] 回忆TechShop的时代，认为课程像是快速浏览多个技能，但要精通某项技能需要更多时间。

• [其他相关课程推荐]
  ◦ [car] 推荐MIT的合成生物学课程"How to Grow (Almost) Anything"，并分享了课程链接。

补充讨论：
• [LarsDu88] 提到PCB设计和从中国定制PCB价格波动的问题，认为美国初创公司有机会填补这一市场空缺。
• [westurner] 指出课程"Week 8: Molding and Casting"的链接404错误，并建议新的材料和科技主题如可编程物质、纳米自组装、AI材料设计等。

争议焦点：
• 课程内容的广度与深度：[moron4hire] 和 [probably_wrong] 认为课程缺乏基础技能和手工技能，而其他人如 [criddell] 和 [zakqwy] 则赞赏课程的创新性和实用性。

44775830.article_content:
My name is D. Sculley.  I lead several teams at Google in
Cambridge doing research in various aspects of machine learning.
I'm involved in this course because many of our current projects involve
the use of machine learning for design or fabrication problems of
one form or another, including in the biology space and the chemistry
space.  I'm interested in learning more about other forms of fabrication
and seeing if there are interesting cross-domain opportunities to
think about.
Here is my
Google Scholar page
, if you're interested in ML papers.
As background, I started working in ML in about 2003.  Before that,
I spent several years in education working as a teacher, and before that
I was a V.E.S. ("art") major in undergrad.
I'll be working on class projects each week, and am planning on making
plenty of mistakes. Always happy to talk about machine learning if that's of interest.
Week 1:
CAD and Sketching
Week 2:
Laser and Vinyl Cutting
Week 3:
Electronics Production
Week 4:
3D Scanning and Printing
Week 5:
Electronics Design
Week 6:
CNC Machining
Week 7:
Embedded Programming
Week 8:
Molding and Casting
Week 9:
Input Devices
Week 10:
Output Devices
Week 11:
Networking
Week 12:
Machine Week
Week 13:
Application Programming
Week 14:
Wildcard Week
Final Project

44776434.article_content:
The Fulbright Program: Chock Full of Bright Ideas
Tags:
academia
,
research
,
musings
Published on
Friday, August 1, 2025
« Previous post:
There is Fun in the Fundamentals
One of the most memorable events in my career so far was being selected
as a host for the
Fulbright Program
.
When
Emily (Simons)
approached me with her idea
of applying for this type of scholarship, I was already blown away by
her enthusiasm—but little did I imagine how immensely enriching her
visit to
the lab
would turn out to be!
We initially discussed a project aligned with our shared interest in
healthcare topics; specifically, I proposed making Emily part of
a planned project with cardiologists, the aim being to study circulatory failure
via certain machine learning methods. The project fell through,
however, since our collaborators were unable to provide data due to
privacy concerns.
1
Hence, we pivoted, and I suggested a couple of
other projects that Emily might be interested in.
Having developed a taste for all things graphs and networks, it was only
a matter of time before Emily started contributing to our work on
physician–patient referral networks
,
showing her skills in data science and visualization. Working together
with
Jeremy (Wayland)
, Emily quickly also got
enthralled by our efforts to better understand
datasets in graph learning. She and Jeremy thus joined a project that
Corinna (Coupette)
and I had been dreaming of
for some time. As an intrepid fellowship, we finally brought it to
fruition as our joint ICML 2025 paper
No Metric to Rule Them All: Toward Principled Evaluations of Graph-Learning Datasets
.
2
This was already outstanding, but Emily did not stop there! Like a
breath of fresh air, she also started working on dissemination strategies for
our projects, improved our repositories, and helped revamp our website.
Watching her grow as a researcher, writer, and software
developer was truly awe-inspiring. And, from what I can
tell, the research stay was rewarding for her as well. New friends, new
colleagues, new experiences—these are things that cannot (and
should not) be easily quantified.
So
why
am I writing all of this? There are two reasons: First, Emily is
on the job market and I cannot sing her praises highly enough. Second,
this is a time of uncertainty; a time in which funding is cut, in
particular for programs that may not yield direct results. Are the
United States richer or better off because of our joint research projects? Probably not—or maybe not
yet
. Like any type of fundamental
research, our projects are but a small part of the grand and eternal
conversation that is science.
It is precisely for this reason that we must resist the urge to see
everything as a
commodity
or as a
fungible good
. The true value of
the Fulbright Program lies in connecting bright minds with others and
giving them new opportunities.
This brings about changes whose
beneficial consequences we cannot possibly fathom in the moment.
To misquote
Boethius
:
And it is because you don’t know the end and purpose of things that
you think these programs have no worth.
Through the Fulbright Program, we all got to meet someone we would not
have met otherwise. Through the Fulbright Program, we created
connections that would not have happened otherwise. Through the
Fulbright Program, we have all been intellectually enriched. I hope
that the politicians responsible for these programs see them for what they
are, i.e., a
unique
opportunity to foster change, innovation, and
mutual understanding across cultural barriers. I, for one, would love to
support such a program.
Let us not sell
tomorrow
in a feeble attempt
to save money
today
.
In my experience, this is the number one reason why research projects fail in Germany; maybe this will be the subject of a subsequent post.
↩︎
For more Tolkien references concerning this work, please read
Emily’s highly engaging blog post
.
↩︎

data.title: The Ski Rental Problem
data.author: skywalqer
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了滑雪租赁问题，这是一个经典的在线算法问题。问题场景是：你去滑雪，但不确定会滑多少天，租滑雪设备每天1单位货币，而购买则需B单位货币。目标是决定是否以及何时购买滑雪设备。

**离线最优算法**：如果提前知道滑雪天数k，当k ≥ B时应购买，k < B时应租。总费用为min{k, B}。

**简单在线算法**：不知道k时，可以先租，直到租金达到B时购买。这种方法的最坏情况成本是两倍于离线最优算法，即竞争比为2。

**随机化算法**：文章进一步探讨了一种随机化算法，通过选择适当的概率分布P(x)，使得期望竞争比接近于$\frac{e}{e-1}$。核心思想是找到一种概率分布，使得期望成本与最优成本的比值（竞争比）不随k变化，从而优化算法性能。经过推导，得出P(x)应为指数分布，满足$\int_0^\infty P(x)dx = 1$。

最终，随机化算法能提供更好的平均性能，适合多次决策场景。

主要讨论点：是否应该购买或租赁滑雪装备，以及如何用数学模型解决决策问题。

不同观点：
• **数学模型的应用**：massung将选择餐馆或电台歌曲的决策问题类比为租赁还是购买滑雪装备的问题，建议使用类似“秘书问题”的数学策略，即先观察前1/3的选项，然后选择下一个不差于最佳选项的方案。这种方法强调通过前期观察来优化决策。

• **实用性与舒适度**：lisbbb认为不需要复杂的数学计算，只要一个季节滑雪超过三次，购买装备就是更优选，因为可以提升舒适度、调整和质量等方面的体验。此外，租用的滑雪装备往往状态不佳。

• **租赁与购买的简单决策规则**：thrawa8387336持简化观点，认为在确定自己需求之前应继续租赁滑雪装备。

• **存储与投资问题**：matchagaucho提到滑雪装备闲置在车库中会成为负担，暗示购买滑雪装备可能导致不必要的存储问题和浪费投资。

• **租赁与购买的成本平衡**：cwmoore提出一种成本平衡的观点，建议当租赁费用累计达到滑雪装备价格的一半时，可以直接购买。

• **季节性租赁方案**：comrade1234推荐像瑞士人一样进行整个季节的租赁，这样每年都能使用新的滑雪装备，同时建议购买定制的滑雪靴。

• **二手市场策略**：rkagerer建议购买滑雪装备后在二手市场出售，以避免长期租赁带来的持续成本（类似软件即服务税）。

• **先验知识的利用**：armanboyaci提到如果对某个选项有先验概率分布知识，如何利用这种信息进行决策。

补充讨论：
• **其他类比问题**：JohnKemeny提出了另一个类似的选择问题，即在等待公交车和步行回家之间的决策，这与滑雪装备的租赁与购买问题类似，但场景不同。

• **安全性考虑**：Tycho提出了对滑雪运动安全性的担忧，将其与骑自行车在公路上的危险性相比较，暗示滑雪运动本身可能存在风险。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于是否需要复杂的数学模型来做出滑雪装备的购买决策。一方认为数学模型可以优化选择，另一方认为实际的舒适度和使用体验更为重要。

44740325.article_content:
Ski Rental Problem
The ski rental problem is a classic example problem in online algorithms. It feels like a small but interesting problem that can be explained relatively easily while some clever tricks can be applied to it.
In this article, I took
these lecture notes
by Debmalya Panigrahi and Hangjie Ji and tried to rewrite them in a way that is easier to understand (at least for me).
Formulation
You are going skiing in the mountains but you are unsure about the weather reports and don't know how many days you will want to ski (and it can be any number of days).
Renting skis costs $1$ unit of currency while buying them costs $B$ units of currency.
The question is whether you should buy skis and on which day.
Optimal offline algorithm
Assuming you wound know the number $k$ of days you will want to ski in advance, an optimal algorithm can be derived.
If $k \geq B$, you should buy the skis and if $k < B$, you should only rent them.
So you will pay $\min\{k, B\}$.
We will need this later, so let's call it $\text{opt}(k) = \min\{k, B\}$.
Simple online algorithm
But what about if you don't know $k$?
A simple algorithm is to buy the skis when you paid $B$ for renting them.
So, the cost is $$\text{alg}(k) = \begin{cases}k & \text{if }k\leq B\\ B+B & \text{if }k>B\end{cases}.$$
We will study the competitive ratio $\rho$ defined as the worst-case ratio of a given online algorithm and the optimal offline algorithm.
$$
\rho_\text{simple} = \max_k \frac{\text{alg(k)}}{\text{opt}(k)} = \max_k \begin{Bmatrix}\frac{k}{k} & \text{if }k \leq B\\ \frac{B+B}{B} & \text{if }k > B\end{Bmatrix} = \max_k \begin{Bmatrix}1 & \text{if }k \leq B\\ 2 & \text{if }k > B\end{Bmatrix} = 2
$$
So, the simple online algorithm is at most two times worse than the offline "future knowing" algorithm.
The randomized algorithm
Let's try to find a better performing randomized algorithm. In fact, an algorithm with $\mathbb{E}[\rho]\approx\frac{e}{e-1}$ exists. This could be useful for example if we do many such decisions and want to do well on average.
In this algorithm, we will buy skis on the $(i+1)$-th day with probability $P_i$. These probabilities should satisfy $\sum_{i=0}^\infty P_i = 1$. We will also assume that the ski buying events are independent.
So when we buy the skis on day $i+1$, we pay $i+B$ if $i < k$ and $k$ if $i \geq k$, thus the expected cost is:
$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right] = k\sum_{i\geq k}P_i + \sum_{i<k}(i+B)P_i
$$
We will approximate this with a continuous probability distribution with probability density $P(x)$:
$$
\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right] \approx k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x
$$
Thus, we have switched from a discrete algorithm to a continuous one, so it will tell us the exact time when to buy instead of some day. With it we will approximate the discrete solution (which also exists but is more complicated to analyze).
Now, we would like to find the optimal probability distribution $P(x)$ such that the competitive ratio $\rho$ is the lowest. We will use an insight which we won't prove. The insight is that the optimal choice is such a distribution $P(x)$ that $\alpha = \frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right]}{\text{opt}(k)}$ does not depend on $k$. Thus, $\mathbb{E}\left[\rho\right] = \max_k\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right]}{\text{opt}(k)} = \max_k\alpha = \alpha$.
So, we have
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\text{alg}(k)\right]}{\text{opt}(k)} &= \alpha \\
k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x &= \alpha\min\{k, B\}
\end{aligned}
$$
And we have two cases,
I) When $k \geq B$
We differentiate both sides with respect to $k$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\global\def\der{\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}k}}
\global\def\Der#1{\frac{\mathrm{d}#1}{\mathrm{d}k}}
k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x &= \alpha B \\
\der\left(k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x\right) &= \Der{\alpha B} \\
\Der{k}\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + k\der\left(\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x\right) + \der\left(\int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x\right) &= 0 \\
\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x - kP(k) + (k+B)P(k) &= 0 \\
\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + BP(k) &= 0
\end{aligned}
$$
Because $P(x) \geq 0$, the integral is nonnegative. And because $B > 0$, the integral must be zero and $P(k) = 0$ in order to satisfy the equation.
II) When $k < B$
We proceed in a similar fashion:
$$
\begin{aligned}
k\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \int_0^k (x+B)P(x)\mathrm{d}x &= \alpha k \\
\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + BP(k) &= \alpha
\end{aligned}
$$
However, now we take the derivative once more:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\der\int_k^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x + \der BP(k) &= \Der{\alpha} \\
B\Der{P(k)} - P(k) &= 0
\end{aligned}
$$
This is a differential equation, which can be solved as $P(k) = Ae^\frac{k}{B}$, where $A$ is some constant.
We have the constraint that $\int_0^\infty P(x)\mathrm{d}x = 1$, so if we combine both cases, we get:
$$
\begin{aligned}

这篇文章讨论了滑雪租赁问题，这是一个经典的在线算法问题。问题场景是：你去滑雪，但不确定会滑多少天，租滑雪设备每天1单位货币，而购买则需B单位货币。目标是决定是否以及何时购买滑雪设备。

**离线最优算法**：如果提前知道滑雪天数k，当k ≥ B时应购买，k < B时应租。总费用为min{k, B}。

**简单在线算法**：不知道k时，可以先租，直到租金达到B时购买。这种方法的最坏情况成本是两倍于离线最优算法，即竞争比为2。

**随机化算法**：文章进一步探讨了一种随机化算法，通过选择适当的概率分布P(x)，使得期望竞争比接近于$\frac{e}{e-1}$。核心思想是找到一种概率分布，使得期望成本与最优成本的比值（竞争比）不随k变化，从而优化算法性能。经过推导，得出P(x)应为指数分布，满足$\int_0^\infty P(x)dx = 1$。

最终，随机化算法能提供更好的平均性能，适合多次决策场景。

data.title: EHRs: The hidden distraction in your doctor's office
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 《Computing Magazine》2025年8月刊文章《医生将查看您的电子健康记录》总结了美国自2004年以来投入超1000亿美元推广电子健康记录（EHR）系统的进展与挑战。文章通过患者Tom的案例，讲述了其妻子Cheryl为获取其医疗记录所经历的困难与如今EHR系统带来的便利。尽管EHR系统在一定程度上实现了医疗信息的集中化，但由于各医疗机构的系统不互通，患者往往拥有多个电子记录，导致新的碎片化问题。此外，EHR系统还面临设计不佳、安全性不足以及医患负担加重等问题。尽管技术进步如AI引入可能带来新机遇，但若不解决现有问题，美国医疗系统可能面临更大挑战。文章强调需更谨慎地推进医疗信息化，以实现布什总统2004年提出的愿景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子健康记录（EHR）系统的使用体验、问题及可能的解决方案

不同观点：
• [jmpz] 认为德国的医生在看病时忙于记录账单项目，导致与患者的互动减少，感觉像是在和机器打交道。这与公共医疗系统中医生工作量过大、患者就诊时间短有关。
• [classichasclass] 持旧式观念，认为在病人面前记录是不礼貌的行为，倾向于在诊后完成记录，且从未在检查室登录EHR系统。
• [brown] 指出EHR系统的一刀切方法往往不适用，定制化成本高且仍不完美。开源平台如Medplum、HAPI或OpenEMR是更好的起点，但医生们仍在寻找更优的解决方案。
• [localghost3000] 分享了自己在医疗技术行业的经验，指出医务人员对新技术常持抵触态度，因为他们更愿意把时间花在病人身上，而非学习新工具。
• [ChrisMarshallNY] 强调EHR系统的用户友好性至关重要，批评当前系统的复杂性和过时设计，并以Apple和Google的成功为例说明简单易用的重要性。
• [AngryData] 认为EHR工具应保持稳定，不频繁更改，以避免对已有工作流程造成干扰，并以机械师和木匠的工具为例说明工具变化带来的困扰。
• [computegabe] 担心EHR系统的安全性，指出自己的医疗记录曾两次被泄露，认为当前系统在安全方面做得不够。
• [dogmatism] 暗示当前医疗系统在技术实施上存在诸多问题，但未详细阐述，仅提到其组织甚至无法实施单点登录。
• [mitchbob] 引用了Atul Gawande的文章，提到有些医生如Neil R. Malhotra在尝试破解EHR系统以改进其功能。
• [onewheeltom] 支持EHR系统的使用，认为虽然对医生来说过渡困难，但对患者而言，能够访问自己的医疗信息是积极的。
• [UltraSane] 强调EHR软件的存在必要性，认为其能够快速搜索和索引健康记录，比纸质记录更有效。
• [osmano807] 详细描述了自己在多个EHR系统中的经验，指出系统间缺乏整合、操作不便、系统崩溃等问题，并提出需要更具灵活性和适应性的EHR系统，可能类似于Linux的开源模式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于EHR系统的用户体验、定制化和安全性问题。一些评论者认为当前系统复杂且难以使用，而另一些评论者则强调工具稳定性的重要性，并指出频繁更改系统可能会带来新的问题。
• 开源平台被视为可能的解决方案之一，但其复杂性和法规遵循问题仍是挑战。
• EHR系统的安全性和数据泄露问题也是讨论的重要方面，亟需更有效的安全措施。
• 医生和技术人员之间的需求差异和沟通障碍在技术推广过程中显现，医务人员更希望将时间花在患者身上而非学习新工具。

44775485.article_content:
Computing
Magazine
Feature
August 2025
“The Doctor Will See Your Electronic Health Record Now”
Since 2004, the U.S. has spent $100 billion for EHR systems that keep doctors glued to their screens
Robert N. Charette
30 Mar 2025
16 min read
iStock/IEEE Spectrum
Red
Cheryl Conrad no longer
seethes with the frustration that threatened to overwhelm her in 2006. As
described
in
IEEE
Spectrum
, Cheryl’s husband, Tom, has a rare genetic disease that causes ammonia to accumulate in his blood. At an emergency room visit two decades ago, Cheryl told the doctors Tom needed an immediate dose of lactulose to avoid going into a coma, but they refused to medicate him until his primary doctor confirmed his medical condition hours later.
Making the situation more vexing was that Tom had been treated at that facility for the same problem a few months earlier, and no one could locate his
medical records
. After Tom’s recovery, Cheryl vowed to always have immediate access to them.
Today, Cheryl says, “Happily, I’m not involved anymore in lugging Tom’s medical records everywhere.” Tom’s two primary medical facilities use the same electronic health record (EHR) system, allowing doctors at both facilities to access his medical information quickly.
In 2004, President George W. Bush set an ambitious goal for U.S.
health care
providers to transition to EHRs by 2014.
Electronic health records
, he declared, would transform health care by ensuring that a person’s complete medical information was
available
“at the time and place of care, no matter where it originates.”
President George W. Bush looks at an electronic medical record system during a visit to the
Cleveland Clinic
on 27 January 2005.
Brooks Kraft/Corbis/Getty Images
Over the next four years, a bipartisan Congress
approved
more than US $150 million in funding aimed at setting up electronic health record demonstration projects and creating the administrative infrastructure needed.
Then, in 2009, during efforts to mitigate the financial crisis, newly elected President
Barack Obama
signed
the $787 billion economic stimulus bill. Part of it contained the
Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act
, also known as the HITECH Act, which
budgeted
$49 billion to promote health
information technology
and EHRs in the
United States
.
As a result, Tom, like most Americans, now has an electronic health record. However, many millions of Americans now have multiple electronic
health records
. On average, patients in the United States
visit
19 different kinds of doctors throughout their lives. Further, many specialists have unique EHR systems that do not automatically communicate
medical data
between each other, so you must update your medical information for each one. Nevertheless, Tom now has immediate access to all his medical treatment and test information, something not readily available 20 years ago.
Tom’s situation underlines the paradox of how far the United States has come since 2004 and how far it still must go to achieve President Bush’s vision of a complete, secure, easily accessible, and seamlessly interoperable lifetime EHR.
As of 2021, nearly 80 percent of physicians and almost all nonfederal acute-care
hospitals
deployed an electronic health record system.
For many patients in the United States today, instead of fragmented, paper medical record silos, they have a plethora of fragmented, electronic medical record silos. And thousands of health care providers are burdened with costly, poorly designed, and insecure EHR systems that have exacerbated clinician burnout, led to hundreds of millions of medical records lost in
data breaches
, and created new sources of medical errors.
EHR’s baseline standardization does help centralize a very fragmented health care system, but in the rush to get EHR systems adopted, key technological and security challenges were overlooked and underappreciated. Subsequently, problems were introduced due to the sheer complexity of the systems being deployed. These still-unresolved issues are now potentially coupled with the unknown consequences of bolting on immature AI-driven technologies. Unless more thought and care are taken now in how to proceed as a fully integrated health care system, we could unintentionally put the entire U.S. health care system in a worse place than when President Bush first declared his EHR goal in 2004.
IT to Correct Health Care Inefficiencies Is a Global Project
Putting government pressure on the health care industry to adopt EHR systems through various financial incentives made sense by the early 2000s. Health care in the United States was in
deep trouble
. Spending increased from $74.1 billion in 1970
to more than
$1.4 trillion by 2000,
2.3 times as fast as the U.S.
gross domestic product.
Health care costs
grew
at three times the rate of inflation from 1990 to 2000 alone, surpassing 13 percent of GDP.
Two major studies conducted by the Institute of Medicine in 2000 and 2001, titled
To Err Is Human

data.title: Yosemite embodies the long war over US national park privatization
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了优胜美地国家公园在美国国家公园私有化争论中的核心角色，以及其历史上私有化和保护之间的冲突。文章提到，优胜美地山谷和马里波萨巨杉林的保护始于1864年，以防止其落入私人手中。然而，早期的土地索赔问题引发了法律纠纷，最终加州政府对索赔者进行了赔偿。尽管1890年优胜美地部分区域成为国家公园，私有利益仍长期存在，私人公司提供住宿和餐饮等服务。历史上，关于在公园内追求利润的争论不断，例如1925年关于建造加油站的争议，以及1930年代滑雪场的建设分歧。文章强调，国家公园私有化和保护之间的矛盾一直未完全解决，至今仍引发关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：国家公园内商业运营的管理不善及其影响

不同观点：
• **bix6**：认为特许经营公司和管理方为了最大化利润而忽视维护责任，导致公园设施维护不善、员工负担过重且人手不足。具体例子提到在加州的某个公园，管理层对员工进行言语甚至身体上的侵犯，且为了节省开支，公园的维护和清洁工作严重不足。

• **terminalshort**：对国家公园内存在商业设施（如杂货店、酒店、加油站）的概念表示反对，认为这与国家公园的初衷相悖。建议将商业开发区域从国家公园中移除并 privatize，以避免利益冲突，同时通过法律禁止在国家公园土地上进行任何开发建设。

• **Johnny555**：引用了一篇新闻报道，指出将历史建筑的维护工作交给以盈利为目的的公司往往会导致建筑得不到妥善维护，进一步支持了对商业运营管理不善的批评。

• **primitivesuave**：以Yosemite为例，指出特许经营公司Aramark在攀岩社区中声誉极差，存在严重疏忽和谎言行为，甚至有高管因不当行为被解雇。然而，由于高端酒店和高价餐饮的盈利机会，政治关系强的公司仍会掌控这些商业机会。

• **lawlessone**：比较了欧洲与美国的户外空间管理，指出欧洲很多伟大的公园是农业和自然森林的结合，希望美国不要重复欧洲的错误，避免将自然区域过度商业化。

• **thrance**：对未来的环境保护持悲观态度，认为尽管当前在努力保护自然环境，但长期来看，商业利益可能最终会占上风，导致自然资源的进一步破坏。

• **WaitWaitWha**：质疑Yosemite的特许经营权为何授予单一公司，认为应通过充分公开的竞争机制选择运营酒店和特许摊位的公司，而不是通过单一来源合同。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于国家公园内商业运营与自然保护之间的平衡问题，特别是商业运营对环境和员工的负面影响。
• 不同评论者对如何解决这一问题提出了不同建议，包括将商业区域私有化、加强法律保护、以及通过竞争机制选择运营方等。
• 对未来环境保护的忧虑也是一个讨论重点，反映了公众对长期可持续发展的关注。

The nation has a long history of similar efforts, including a wildly unpopular 1980 attempt by Reagan administration Interior Secretary James Watt to
promote development and expand private concessions
in the parks. But debate over using public national park land for private profit dates back more than a century before that.
As I explain in
my forthcoming book
, no park has played a more central role in that debate than Yosemite, in California.
Early concerns
In early 1864, Central American Steamship Transit Company representative Israel Ward Raymond wrote a letter to John Conness, a U.S. senator from California,
urging the government to move swiftly
to preserve the Yosemite Valley and the Mariposa Grove of giant sequoia trees to prevent them from falling into private hands. Five months later, President Abraham Lincoln signed the Yosemite Grant Act, ceding the valley and the grove to the state of California, “upon the express conditions that the premises shall be
held for public use, resort, and recreation
.” This was years before Yellowstone became the
first federal land designated a national park
in 1872.
For centuries, the natural beauty of the Yosemite Valley has impressed visitors.
Sepia Times/Universal Images Group via Getty Images
Controversy arose quickly at Yosemite. Two men – James Lamon and James Hutchings – had
claimed land in the valley
before the federal government gave it to California. Both began commercial operations,
Lamon growing cash crops
and
Hutchings operating a hotel
.
California said their businesses threatened the state’s ability to develop roads and trails in Yosemite by competing for tourist dollars. A legal battle ensued and was not resolved until an
1872 U.S. Supreme Court ruling
found that the men’s land claims had not been fully validated according to the procedures of the time. The California legislature
paid both men compensation for their land
, and both left the park.
In 1890,
neighboring parts of the Yosemite area
became America’s third national park – and in 1906, the federal government again took possession of the Yosemite Valley itself and the Mariposa Grove, specifically to
incorporate them into an expansion of the national park
.
Development rights
Yet, as my research has found, the role of private interests in the park remained unsolved. Private companies under contract to the National Park Service have long provided needed amenities
such as lodging and food
within the national parks. But questions over what is acceptable in national parks in the pursuit of profit have shaped Yosemite’s history for generations.
In 1925, I found, the question centered on the right to build the first gas station inside the park, in Yosemite Valley. Two private businesses, the Curry Camping Company and the Yosemite National Park Company, had long competed for tourist dollars within the park. Each wanted to build a gas station to boost profits.
Frustrated over the need to decide
, National Park Service Director Horace Albright ordered the rival firms to simplify management of the park’s concessions. The companies merged, and the newly formed Yosemite Park and Curry Company was granted the exclusive rights to run lodges, restaurants and other facilities within the park, including the new gas station.
But as I found in my research, the park service and the concessions company did not always see eye to eye on the purpose of the park. The conflict between profit and preservation is perhaps most clearly illustrated by the construction of a ski area within the park in the early 1930s. The park service initially opposed the development of Badger Pass Ski Area as
not conducive to the national park ideal
, but the Yosemite Park and Curry Company insisted it was key to boosting winter use of the park.

44778087.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了优胜美地国家公园在美国国家公园私有化争论中的核心角色，以及其历史上私有化和保护之间的冲突。文章提到，优胜美地山谷和马里波萨巨杉林的保护始于1864年，以防止其落入私人手中。然而，早期的土地索赔问题引发了法律纠纷，最终加州政府对索赔者进行了赔偿。尽管1890年优胜美地部分区域成为国家公园，私有利益仍长期存在，私人公司提供住宿和餐饮等服务。历史上，关于在公园内追求利润的争论不断，例如1925年关于建造加油站的争议，以及1930年代滑雪场的建设分歧。文章强调，国家公园私有化和保护之间的矛盾一直未完全解决，至今仍引发关注。

data.title: My bytecode optimizer beats Copilot by 2x
data.author: top256
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了作者开发的侧项目SuperVM，一个专用于优化字节码和机器码的工具，与通用大语言模型（LLM）不同，SuperVM使用确定性系统和形式化证明进行优化，而非概率推断。在一个简单的分形生成器提速实验中，SuperVM在帧率（FPS）上显著优于GPT-4o等通用模型，达到99.8 FPS，而GPT-4o为49.3 FPS，原始代码仅13.8 FPS。实验显示，尽管LLM在代码生成上有优势，但在代码优化方面，SuperVM凭借直接编辑字节码和更可靠的优化技术表现更佳。文章强调了专用工具相较于通用工具在特定任务上的优势，并指出两者具有互补性。所有代码已发布在Github上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）与专用工具/优化器在代码优化和执行效率上的比较

不同观点：
• farkin88认为，关键不在于生成更好的提示，而在于语义上的保证。通过在字节码层面验证无副作用，可以安全地进行优化，而LLM由于无法验证不变量，无法进行此类优化，从而导致性能差距。
• gsoltis提出，是否可以将这种优化器与LLM结合使用，或者将计算出的不变量作为MCP暴露出来。
• dhosek指出，专用工具通常优于通用工具，因为它们是为特定任务优化的，这是理所当然的。
• amelius认为，不应对专用工具表现更好感到意外，但LLM开发者正在学习和改进，未来可能会解决这些问题，不过可能不会感谢/信用原作者。
• furyofantares表示，虽然人类可能表现更好，但仅通过一次性提示来展示这一点并不合适，应该使用更复杂的测试环境。
• 44za12分享了自己的经验，尝试使用多个LLM来加速代码，但尚未成功，并邀请他人提供建议。
• cr125rider简单表达了编译器仍然优于LLM的观点。
• Lockal认为，LLM可能会剽窃现有优化代码，并且专用优化器受限于特定领域，而图形任务本应在GPU上解决。
• bastawhiz怀疑，如果作者提示模型编写一个优化器，可能会得到更好的结果，而不是仅仅提示优化代码。
• Kuinox质疑作者使用的LLM模型，并指出不同模型可能会有不同的表现。
• lawlessone提醒，LLM在使用相同提示和种子时仍然是确定性的，这可能影响测试结果。
• UncleEntity建议，通过将所有代码运行在字节码优化器上进行对比测试，可能会是更公平的比较方式。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及LLM与专用工具的性能对比，包括编译器优化和特定任务的优化。
• 争议的焦点在于LLM是否能通过学习和改进达到或超过专用工具的性能，以及如何公平地测试和比较两者。
• 提出了结合使用LLM和专用工具的可能性，以及改进测试方法的建议。
• 不同评论者对LLM的当前能力和未来潜力持不同看法，有些持乐观态度，有些则持怀疑态度。

44747786.article_content:
Even amid the AGI race, a specialized tool really outperforms general‑purpose models. And even when this specialized tool is a side-project and at a very early stage.
I am building as a side-project a tool called SuperVM. It optimizes bytecode and machine code similarly to how a LLM would do but instead of using statistical systems, it uses deterministic systems and reasons from facts instead of probabilities (nothing new here these things have been around forever).
All the generated code is available on
Github
.
Experiment
I coded a very simple, hand-coded
fractal generator
.
The code is deliberately kept small and simple because that’s what coding agents handle best. We already know they struggle with large codebases.
Then I gave each Copilot the same one‑line prompt:
“make it faster.”
Result
I measured the average FPS (frame per second) after 99 frames have been displayed.
Model
Average FPS
Original
13.8
Sonnet
39
GPT4o
49.3
SuperVM
99.8
Original (13.8 FPS)
Copilot GPT 4o (49.3 FPS)
SuperVM (99.8 FPS)
Limitations
All numbers are cold‑start FPS; no JIT warm‑up for any variant. No JMH.
SuperVM compiled the fractal in seconds while Copilots run for a few minutes.
I tested different prompts but the simple one was the best.
For the AI, I picked the best out of 10 codegen for each. I didn’t do that for SuperVM (but the output is deterministic so it wasn’t warranted).
Why supervm wins
SuperVM
edits
bytecode directly
and leverages
formal proofs
. That gives it access to broader and more reliable optimization techniques.
Original Code
Original Code
ChatGPT found an embarassingly parallel loop and applied a
parallel()
on it.
ChatGPT-4o generated code
SuperVM proved that the pixel‑iteration loop was side‑effect‑free, split it into
n
long-running worker threads, and inserted an order‑preserving queue so the GUI’s
repaint()
still runs sequentially. It did more work and understood
SuperVM decompiled dequeuing for repaint
SuperVM long running thread
Again, all the generated code is available on
Github
.
conclusions
Of course, the experimental setup is too narrow to draw sweeping conclusions but these
textbook‑size
programs are exactly where LLMs ought to shine. And they don’t.  SuperVM clearly wins by doubling the frame-rate while compiling in seconds.
This point
s
to the limit of general tool vs. specialized tools and how they actually complement each other.
LMs are brilliant at
creating
code.
SuperVM optimizes the code through reasoning from the byte‑code
.
This complementary fascinates me and I’ll test SuperVM on a more general benchmark as soon as I have a little bit of time outside of my day job.
And also I’m curious if it can optimize inference serving. After all loop parallelization is the bread and butter of MLIR and it seems that this tool goes much further than state of the art.

data.title: Life, Work, Death and the Peasant: Family Formation
data.author: Khaine
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于前现代农民的婚姻模式，他们是前工业社会中的大多数人口。文章首先回顾了前现代社会的高死亡率，尤其是婴儿、儿童和产妇的死亡率，导致平均预期寿命较低。在这种背景下，婚姻是家庭形成的第一步，且几乎人人都被期望结婚生子。尽管婚姻在不同文化中存在差异，但前现代社会的婚姻普遍率很高。需要注意的是，精英阶层的婚姻模式与农民显著不同，精英往往因为家族联盟和继承需求而更早结婚。文章特别提到，中世纪西欧的普通农民结婚年龄相对较晚，女性约二十多岁，男性则接近三十岁。理解这些婚姻模式对于认识前现代社会的家庭结构至关重要。

• officehero则积极推荐Bret Devereaux，认为他对古代世界的历史分析真实而直接，并提到在YouTube上发现他的视频，是对低质量信息泛滥的网络环境的一种 refreshing break。

44765562.article_content:
Bret Devereaux
Collections
,
The Peasant
August 1, 2025
27 Minutes
This is the first part of the third part of our series (
I
,
II
) discussing the patterns of life of the pre-modern peasants who made up the great majority of all humans who lived in our agrarian past and indeed a majority of all humans
who have ever lived
.
1
Last week, we looked at death, examining the brutal mortality regime of pre-modern societies, typified by extremely high (c. 50%) infant and child mortality, very high maternal mortality and often high male military mortality, which kept life expectancy
at birth
as low as the mid twenties, while life expectancy at adulthood was better – around 50 – but still very low by modern standards.
This week and next, we’ll start working out some of the consequences of this mortality regime, looking at family formation which in these pre-modern agrarian societies means marriage.  While the intense variability of mortality meant that peasant households came in a variety of single- and multi-family forms, pre-modern agrarian societies generally had strict and rigid expectations for marriage: in nearly all of these societies
everyone
got married and was expected to get around to having children
because the community required them
rather than necessarily because they wanted to.
So this week we’re going to look at marriage patterns, particularly the question of age at first marriage.  Then next week, we’re going to turn to the implications those patterns have for child-bearing and child-rearing.
The family and the household were the fundamental institutions of everyday life for pre-modern people, so understanding their structures and assumptions is crucial for understanding the rest of life in these past societies
.
But first, if you like what you are reading, please share it and if you
really
like it, you can support this project on
Patreon
! While I do teach as the academic equivalent of a tenant farmer, tilling the Big Man’s classes, this project is my little plot of freeheld land which enables me to keep working as a writers and scholar. And if you want updates whenever a new post appears, you can click below for email updates or follow me on
Twitter
and
Bluesky
and (less frequently) Mastodon (@bretdevereaux@historians.social) for updates when posts go live and my general musings; I have largely shifted over to Bluesky (I maintain some
de minimis
presence on Twitter), given that it has become a much better place for historical discussion than Twitter.
Email Address
Subscribe!
Marriage, Marriage is What Brings Us Together, Today
Mawwiage, mawwiage is what brings us together, today.
No, I will not apologize for this joke.
We begin with marriage as the first step in
family
formation (though not necessarily
household
formation, as we’ll see).
Whereas the pre-modern mortality regime is broadly consistent over different cultures, marriage patterns (nuptiality) vary significantly
.  Very nearly all human cultures practice something we can identify as marriage, the mostly-permanent pair-bonding of individuals to create a new family (but not necessarily household) unit into which new children are born.  Different cultures, even in the pre-modern world, differ notably on the
rate
of marriage (though it is, in all cases, by modern standards very high, for reasons which will become clear), its
timing
, and the presence or absence of polygamy.
Before we get into those variables though, we need to make a very important point:
we are talking about peasants.
Remember peasants?  This is a post about peasants.
The marriage patterns of high elites in a society are often quite different from the marriage patterns of most of the society
.  The
classic example of this
is to note that students are often mislead by European aristocrats in the medieval and early modern periods marrying
very
young and so they assume that
everyone
in medieval Europe married very young, but in fact, as we’ll see in a moment, medieval western Europe is notable for
very late
(mid-twenties for women, late twenties for men) typical age at first marriage among the general population.
The very wealthy do not marry under the same economic constraints and incentives as the enormous majority (upwards of 90%) of the population living as peasant farmers
or even the smaller subset working in cities or having specialized trades or so on.  Indeed
it is
very common
for elites in pre-industrial societies to marry
much
younger than non-elites
, because of the different pressures (family alliances, the need for heirs, the lack of direct economic pressure) placed on those marriage decisions.
Via the British Museum (

44765562.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于前现代农民的婚姻模式，他们是前工业社会中的大多数人口。文章首先回顾了前现代社会的高死亡率，尤其是婴儿、儿童和产妇的死亡率，导致平均预期寿命较低。在这种背景下，婚姻是家庭形成的第一步，且几乎人人都被期望结婚生子。尽管婚姻在不同文化中存在差异，但前现代社会的婚姻普遍率很高。需要注意的是，精英阶层的婚姻模式与农民显著不同，精英往往因为家族联盟和继承需求而更早结婚。文章特别提到，中世纪西欧的普通农民结婚年龄相对较晚，女性约二十多岁，男性则接近三十岁。理解这些婚姻模式对于认识前现代社会的家庭结构至关重要。

data.title: Writing a good design document
data.author: kiyanwang
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了如何撰写优秀的设计文档。设计文档是一份技术报告，旨在根据权衡和限制条件，说明系统的实施策略。其目标是让读者相信该设计在给定情况下是最优的，而最需要说服的其实是作者本人。撰写过程有助于澄清模糊的想法，揭示思维中的漏洞。

文档的组织至关重要，应避免写成“意大利面条式”的杂乱无章。好的文档应让读者感觉顺理成章，毫无意外。为此，作者需预见并解决可能的异议，引导读者从当前认知到达认同设计的目标。

编辑时应尽量简化文字，删除不必要的词句，以节省读者注意力。多加练习是关键，像亚马逊这样的公司有浓厚的文档文化，有助于提升写作能力。具体技巧包括使用短段落，将文档视作连贯的要点序列。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：设计文档的目标和最佳实践

不同观点：
• [nickm12] 认为设计文档的目标不是追求最优方案，而是提供足够的解决方案。他强调设计是在约束和权衡之间做出选择，文档应清楚地展示这些选择，并说明为何选择某一方案而非其他替代方案。他不认为设计能消除所有潜在问题，但应尽量降低风险并与利益相关者有效沟通。

• [patrickmay] 强调设计文档的重要性，引用"Writing is nature's way of telling us how sloppy our thinking is"来表明写作有助于澄清思路。他推荐了一篇关于如何提升技术写作质量的文章，并认为即使在行业内多年的人也常常忽视设计文档的重要性。

• [B-Con] 作为设计审查者，认为设计文档应简化复杂问题，不应包含所有困难和错误的细节。他主张文档应使复杂事物简单化，并将不必要的细节放到附录中。

• [farkin88] 指出设计文档批准后可能面临的维护问题，建议使用轻量级的架构决策记录（ADRs）来跟踪上下文和决策状态，以防止设计文档随着时间推移失效。

• [mtlynch] 对亚马逊会议中让参与者在会上阅读文档的做法提出质疑，认为这浪费了宝贵的会议时间。他认为文档应在会前阅读，会议应专注于讨论。

• [ryanmadden] 强调文档的组织和清晰度是软件工程师提升文档写作能力的主要障碍，并讨论了段落长度和信息密度的问题。他分享了自己在谷歌的经验，并提到不同公司可能有不同的文档写作实践。

• [Scarblac] 询问是否有好的设计文档集合，表示在其职业生涯中很少见到优秀的设计文档。

• [cadamsdotcom] 提出使用LLM（大语言模型）来帮助文档写作，建议通过多次简化和修改来提高文档质量。

• [lastdong] 强调通过技术写作课程提高了总结文档的能力，提倡使用“红色笔”方法来减少不必要的词语，并指出这是一项需要定期训练的技能。

• [norseboar] 认为有些读者只想知道结论而不关心推理过程，因此文档应先给出结论以满足这些读者的需求。

• [codemac] 介绍了两种文档结构方法：B.O.O.（背景、目标、概述）和Good Strategy/Bad Strategy（问题诊断、指导方针/假设/需求、行动），并指出不同方法适用于不同情境。

• [kator] 分享了在亚马逊工作7.5年的经验，强调从客户需求出发撰写PRFAQs并收集反馈，即使在个人项目中也坚持这种做法。

• [matt-p] 提到有时会为自己编写设计文档，认为这种方式非常有效，并希望能看到示例文档以作比较。

• [alphazard] 强调在有写作和设计文化的公司工作的重要性，认为工程师应优先选择有书面计划的项目，并避免没有书面计划的领导和项目。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：设计文档是否应包含所有细节还是仅给出结论。例如，[B-Con] 和 [norseboar] 对文档应包含多少细节有不同看法。
• 实用建议：包括使用LLM帮助文档写作（[cadamsdotcom]），通过技术写作课程提升能力（[lastdong]），以及使用ADRs维护文档（[farkin88]）。
• 文档结构和风格：不同评论者提出了多种文档结构和写作风格的建议，如B.O.O.方法（[codemac]）和Good Strategy/Bad Strategy方法（[codemac]）。

总体来看，讨论围绕设计文档的目的、内容、结构和写作技巧展开，参与者分享了各自的经验和建议。

44779428.article_content:
How to write a good design document
This essay is a version of
the response
I gave to my friend Vik's call for suggestions:
had a lot of people ask how they can learn to write design docs, and i didn’t have a good answer besides “work at a place with writing culture and smart senior engineers”. anyone have more useful advice?
https://t.co/7F9BV31shv
— vik (@vikhyatk)
August 31, 2024
Definition
A design document is a technical report that outlines the implementation strategy of a system in the context of trade-offs and constraints.
Goal
Think of a design document like a proof in mathematics. The goal of a proof is to convince the reader that the theorem is true. The goal of a design document is to convince the reader the design is optimal given the situation.
The most important person to convince is
the author
. The act of writing a design document helps to add rigor to what are otherwise vague intuitions. Writing reveals how sloppy your thinking was (and later, code will show how sloppy your writing was).
Organization
Good design document organization is as important as code organization. You probably have opinions about code organization. You've probably used the phrase "spaghetti code" to describe poorly-organized code. Most programmers write "spaghetti design docs" unless they've had a lot of practice.
Let me illustrate a common code organization issue some programmers run into on their first day. The novice writes
terminal.print("Hello world")
Then they decide they want to make the text red, so they edit their program to
terminal.print("Hello world")
terminal.setPrintColor("red")
And then they're confused that it didn't come out red. They haven't internalized that the first line of code
happens before
the second. They just get a soup of code on the screen that kind of has the ingredients for a program, and expect the computer to do what they want.
Novice document writers make the
exact
same mistake, but with prose instead of code. They get a soup of sentences and paragraphs and expect the reader's brain to do what they want.
If the reader is smart enough, you might actually get away with this. Just like an expert programmer can mentally untangle spaghetti code.
But a perfect doc is written such that the reader
is never surprised
. The reader should find that every sentence flows obviously from the previous ones. They should finish your doc and think "well this was entirely straightforward, why did we even need to have this meeting?".
This disappoints the ego-seeking behavior of many engineers. Good engineers often want people to realize how clever they were.
But a good doc will lay out the problem and mental models in a way that the solution that took weeks of hard thought to invent will be clear to the reader by the time the doc presents it.
This also requires having a good model of the minds of the people reading your doc. The goal of your doc is to take their minds from their current state to a new state in which they believe your design is a good one.
You should anticipate every objection someone would have and preemptively show why it's invalid, so that the reader never even thinks to bring it up.
Many engineers fail at modeling the starting state of their readers' minds, so fail at getting them to the destination state.
Editing
Once you've got the information organized and laid out properly, the next step is to edit for length. Remove every word that can be removed. Do this because your readers' attention is a scarce resource.
Unless you're an unusually terse writer, you can almost always cut length by ~30% from the first draft without sacrificing information.
The easiest way to get good at editing by going through
other
people's docs with a red pen and crossing out unnecessary words. You'll find tons. It's easier to criticize other people.
Once you've built this muscle, you can turn the weapon on yourself. Distilling thoughts to fit into the 280 character tweet limit is also surprisingly good practice.
Volume
There's no substitute for lots of practice. I'm grateful for having worked at AWS with a unique doc-writing culture. The first docs I wrote there were terrible, but after a few hundred, I like to think they were pretty good.
For unfamiliar readers: Amazon meetings start with the presenter passing out copies (historically physical, though increasingly digital since Covid) of a prose document. The document is 1-6 pages depending on the importance.
The meeting starts with everyone sitting in silence, reading the document, and adding notes and questions in the margins with red pen. Watching people mark up the document you spent so much time polishing is a
strong
forcing function to become a better writer.
Concrete tips
These work for me, but they may not work for you.
Use short paragraphs
You should think of your doc as a series of bullet points that flow into each other. That is, a doc might be organized like:
Observation A
Observation B
Because B, idea C
But problems D and E
Observation F
Ther

data.title: This Old SGI: notes and memoirs on the Silicon Graphics 4D series (1996)
data.author: exvi
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是A. J. Corda编写的关于修复和维护SGI 4D系列机器的经验笔记，包含系统安装、硬件配置、故障排查等详细信息。主要内容包括：不同SGI系统的配置与性能、图形设置、串口连接、电源问题、实时时钟与非易失性内存问题、音频能力、硬件调试技巧等。此外，文章还介绍了如何绕过NVRAM密码、恢复格式化磁盘、构建可引导的IRIX文件系统等技术细节。作者提到，通过Usenet获取信息的重要性，并建议在未收到回复时重新审视问题，而不要急于重新发布帖子。文章旨在分享作者的经验，回馈网络社区的帮助。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对SGI（Silicon Graphics, Inc.）老式工作站的怀旧与技术讨论，以及对SGI未实现的潜在发展的想象。

不同观点：
• **lastdong**：认为如今能够在家中使用到相当于SGI级别机器（得益于Nvidia的技术进步）是非常了不起的。他提到了之前在Hacker News上讨论过的相关话题，暗示技术的进步让人印象深刻。

• **fidotron**：分享了自己拥有一个罕见的老式4D/60 "buttons box"的经历，并提到与现代设备对接的困难。他还回忆了以前使用Indigo工作站的经历，强调了老式设备与现代设备兼容性的问题。此外，他提到了一段为VR公司工作的经历，强调了老技术人员对电力供应的重视。

• **JSR_FDED**：回忆了自己修复一台在火灾中受损的Indigo2 Max Impact工作站的经历，表达了对拥有这种高端设备的自豪感，并认为IRIX 4Dwm桌面系统即便在今天也毫不逊色。

• **t1234s**：强调了O2工作站的设计巧妙之处，特别是其组件易于更换的特点。

• **aa-jv**：作为一个SGI的忠实粉丝，他分享了自己从MIPS Magnum到SGI Indy，再到Octane2和O2的设备使用经历。他提出了一个假设性的问题：如果SGI当年推出了一款笔记本电脑，生活会是什么样子？并认为这将像当年的Apple tiBook一样具有革命性。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到了SGI老式工作站的技术成就和设计独特性，尤其是其与现代设备的兼容性问题和电力需求。
• 讨论还涉及了SGI潜在的发展路径，尤其是关于如果SGI推出笔记本电脑可能会带来的影响，暗示了对技术发展不同路径的想象和怀旧情感。
• 争议的焦点可能在于对老式技术价值的看法，一些人认为这些老设备即便在今天也具有竞争力，而另一些人可能更关注其与现代技术的兼容性和实用性。

I am posting this assortment of notes and observations as
a kind of "thank you" to the numerous people who have replied
to my posts in the past.  The free flow of information is
the life-blood of the internet community, and this is my feeble
attempt to maintain that flow, while at the same time repaying
the kindness shown me by other members of the community in my
rather obsessive attempts to revive a defunct 4D professional

I have posted a number of messages concerning my project, and
I can say that all the replies I have received have been quite
helpful. One of the things you learn early on as a denizen of
the net is the utility of Usenet posts. You also learn that
the volume of answers can convey almost as much information
as the content of those answers. If I post a question and
receive a significant number of replies, then I can be relatively
certain that others have run across (and possibly solved) the
same class of problem. If, however, I receive no responses, it
indicates that this is a new problem not previously encountered

the problem represents a true hardware-level failure (usually
at the IC level) or the problem is due to some fundamental stupidity
on my part (by far the most likely scenario!). This means that
it's time to re-evaluate the procedure which caused the problem,
which usually leads to an alternate approach which inevitably
works. During this project, I have only had 2 genuine hardware
